- [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?

Fix fused local `ColumnParallelLinear` / `RowParallelLinear` weight-gradient accumulation under Megatron-FSDP v1. Two microbatches contributing 8 and 96 per weight must produce 104; the existing local backward overwrites the first contribution and produces 96.

The local backward now reads FSDP's per-parameter `overwrite_main_grad` policy through an explicit `accumulate` variable. FSDP initializes that policy immediately after buffer creation, covering pure `no_shard` without FSDP units; its existing unshard-time refresh is retained.

`TEGroupedMLP._ensure_main_grad` also preserves the policy while exposing fused-op buffers. Previously it forced the flag to `True`, undoing the initialization on paths without an unshard hook. Existing `False`/`True` values and an absent attribute are preserved.

## Issue tracking

Fixes #8332.

## Validation

Base: `ce852bfb93f364f64a556602fc71a5d9ed2c377e`; tested head: `66925cb281602ff0a830ff9e72f2ba9b9eacd673`.
Environment: H200, Python 3.12, PyTorch `2.10.0a0+b558c986e8.nv25.11`, CUDA 13.0, Transformer Engine `2.18.0+27486e0`; TP/CP/EP=1 and FP32 main gradients.

The numerical regression exercises both the local writer alone and the real MoE preparation helper before that writer. Both paths use actual FSDP buffers and TE wgrad GEMM. It covers four sharding strategies, FP32/BF16 parameters, `no_shard` with/without FSDP units, and two accumulation cycles separated by `zero_grad_buffer()`.

| Test / validation | Scope / environment | Result | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| FSDP accumulation matrix | 1 H200; local and MoE-helper paths | 20/20 passed; exact 104/152 across two cycles | `test_local_linear_fused_wgrad_accumulation` |
| FSDP accumulation matrix | 8 H200; actual gradient sharding | 20/20 on every rank: 160 rank-test passes; exact gradients | Same test; all 8 rank reports checked |
| Historical MoE-policy negative control | 1 H200; FP32/BF16, `no_shard`, no unit | Both fail as expected: 256/256 entries wrong, max absolute error 8 | Restore only the previous PR helper in memory; details below |
| MoE pre-forward hook policy | Existing `False`, `True`, and absent attribute; CPU tensors | 3/3 passed; buffer identity and disabled-fusion path also checked | `test_make_fused_impl_pre_forward_hook_exposes_fsdp_main_grad_for_fused_wgrad` |
| Wgrad and expert-policy determinism | FP32/BF16, overwrite/accumulate, FP32 output, side-stream contention | 8/8 passed; 3 bit-exact replays each | `test_fsdp_wgrad_gemm_replays`; `test_expert_main_grad_policy_replays` |
| Formatting / determinism coverage | All 7 changed Python files | Black, isort, Pylint, Ruff and kernel coverage gate passed | `tools/autoformat.sh`; `tools/check_kernel_determinism_coverage.py` |
| Static typing | mypy 2.4.0; autoformatter's non-gating step | Tool internal error; no passing type-check claim | `error: INTERNAL ERROR` |
| Full TEGroupedMLP op-fuser probe | Separate exploratory 5-configuration probe with the same runtime edits | All 5 failed at backend setup before gradient comparison | TE compiled with cuBLAS 13.1; grouped GEMM requires 13.3+ |
| Initial negative-control launcher | After 20 single-rank numerical passes | Aborted before control test collection on Git ownership check; fixed and remaining checks rerun | Scoped `safe.directory` for reading historical helper; successful controls above |
| Full-model / other parallelism | Training curves, optimizer/checkpoint integration, TP/CP/EP > 1 | Not run | Focused buffer-policy validation; full op-fuser numerics remain unvalidated |
| Commit signatures | All 3 commits | DCO + SSH signatures; local verification passes | GitHub reports `unknown_key`; the current token cannot register signing keys |

Totals at the tested head: **51 pytest configurations / 191 rank-test passes**, plus **2 expected negative-control failures**. The totals combine 20 numerical passes retained from the initial validation run and 171 passes from the follow-up run; both used the identical runtime/test commit above. Every rank's setup, call, and teardown reports were checked. The final follow-up job and its replica both reached `Succeeded`.

<details>
<summary>Focused commands, numerical controls, and limitations</summary>

Equivalent focused pytest commands are shown below. The validation launcher additionally records each rank's pytest reports, rejects missing/skipped calls, and checks subprocess exit codes.

```bash
export NVIDIA_TF32_OVERRIDE=0
export CUDA_DEVICE_MAX_CONNECTIONS=1
export CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:4096:8

# Run with both --nproc-per-node=1 and --nproc-per-node=8.
python3 -m torch.distributed.run --standalone --nproc-per-node=8 \
  -m pytest -q -o addopts=-rA -p no:cacheprovider \
  --confcutdir=tests/unit_tests/distributed/mfsdp_v1 \
  tests/unit_tests/distributed/mfsdp_v1/test_mfsdp_fully_shard.py::TestMegatronFsdpFullyShard::test_local_linear_fused_wgrad_accumulation

python3 -m torch.distributed.run --standalone --nproc-per-node=1 \
  -m pytest -q -o addopts=-rA -p no:cacheprovider \
  --confcutdir=tests/unit_tests/transformer/moe \
  tests/unit_tests/transformer/moe/test_grouped_mlp.py::test_make_fused_impl_pre_forward_hook_exposes_fsdp_main_grad_for_fused_wgrad

python3 -m torch.distributed.run --standalone --nproc-per-node=1 \
  -m pytest -q -o addopts=-rA -p no:cacheprovider \
  --confcutdir=tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels \
  tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels/test_tensor_parallel_kernels.py::test_fsdp_wgrad_gemm_replays \
  tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels/test_moe_kernels.py::test_expert_main_grad_policy_replays

python3 tools/check_kernel_determinism_coverage.py --base-ref origin/main
CHECK_ONLY=true bash tools/autoformat.sh
```

The negative controls load only `TEGroupedMLP._ensure_main_grad` from the previous PR head, `fd466d12582ee2f6e896a3f2176bc18e95a3fedf`, into memory and select the two `moe-hook` / `no_shard` / no-unit cases. Both dtypes reproduce 96 instead of 104, with all 256 entries differing by 8. The fixed helper passes the complete one-rank and eight-rank matrices, including reset behavior in the second cycle.

`--confcutdir` avoids unrelated global data-download fixtures. Overriding `addopts` avoids the installed pytest duration reporter's session-completion error; test assertions remain enabled.

The full grouped-MLP probe reached the real TE op-fuser but stopped in `nvte_get_grouped_gemm_setup_workspace_size`, which requires cuBLAS 13.3+ while this TE extension was compiled with 13.1. Passing numerical evidence therefore covers the real MoE helper, FSDP lifecycle, and TE local wgrad GEMM; a compatible grouped-GEMM build is still needed to validate full `TEGroupedMLP` op-fuser numerics. That environment-dependent exploratory test is outside the committed diff.

</details>

## Contribution process

### Pre-checks

- [x] I have added relevant unit tests.
- [ ] I have added relevant functional tests — focused distributed numerical validation only; full-model training was not run.
- [x] I have added bit-exact determinism tests in the already registered tensor-parallel and MoE kernel test files; the coverage gate passes.
- [x] I have added proper typing to my code — no new public API or changed signatures.
- [x] I have added relevant documentation — inline policy rationale and test docstrings.
- [x] I have run `tools/autoformat.sh` — Black/isort/Pylint/Ruff pass; the non-gating mypy step has the internal error recorded above.

### Code review

Requires FSDP, MoE, and tensor-parallel owner review of persistent-buffer accumulation versus per-backward gradient reduction. The existing unshard-time policy refresh is retained.

nodes.body:
One case to check before dropping it: `TEGroupedMLP._ensure_main_grad` (`megatron/core/transformer/moe/experts.py`, from #5209) sets `overwrite_main_grad = True` on the expert weights in the op-fuser pre-forward hook whenever `fuse_wgrad_accumulation` is on and the attribute exists. When the unshard hooks run, for example with `optim` and FSDP units, the pre-backward gather resets the attribute to `_reduces_grad_every_backward(param)` before the fused wgrad reads it. Without the hook-time assignment, those expert wgrads would overwrite `main_grad` instead of accumulating across microbatches.

With this PR, the same thing can already happen under pure `no_shard`. The attribute now exists from construction, `_ensure_main_grad` flips it to `True`, and no hook resets it. Keeping the per-parameter policy in `_ensure_main_grad` instead of forcing `True` would cover both cases and make the hook-time assignment redundant. `test_make_fused_impl_pre_forward_hook_exposes_fsdp_main_grad_for_fused_wgrad` currently asserts the forced value.

I found this by reading the code; I haven't run the op-fuser grouped-MLP path.

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("dtype", (torch.float32, torch.bfloat16))
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("overwrite_main_grad", (False, True))
+def test_expert_main_grad_policy_replays(dtype, overwrite_main_grad):
+    """Expert buffer preparation preserves overwrite/accumulation across GEMM replays."""
+    from megatron.core.tensor_parallel.layers import _wgrad_gemm
+
+    seeded()
+    linear = torch.nn.Linear(64, 128, bias=False, device="cuda", dtype=dtype)
+    linear.fuse_wgrad_accumulation = True
+    linear.weight.overwrite_main_grad = overwrite_main_grad
+    initial_grad = torch.ones(128, 64, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32)
+    inputs = tuple(
+        torch.randint(0, 4, shape, device="cuda").to(dtype)
+        for shape in ((32, 64), (32, 128), (64, 64), (64, 128))
+    )
+
+    def write_grads(main_grad, x1, dy1, x2, dy2):
+        linear.weight.main_grad = None
+        linear.weight.get_main_grad = lambda: main_grad
+        for x, dy in ((x1, dy1), (x2, dy2)):
+            TEGroupedMLP._ensure_main_grad(linear)
+            _wgrad_gemm(
+                linear.weight.main_grad, dy, x, accumulate=not linear.weight.overwrite_main_grad
+            )
+        return main_grad
+
+    outputs, _ = assert_replays_bit_exact(
+        write_grads,
+        (initial_grad, *inputs),
+        backward=False,
+        contention=True,
+        replays=3,
+        what=f"expert main_grad[{dtype}, overwrite={overwrite_main_grad}]",
+    )
+    x1, dy1, x2, dy2 = inputs
+    expected = dy2.float().T @ x2.float()
+    if not overwrite_main_grad:
+        expected += initial_grad + dy1.float().T @ x1.float()
+    torch.testing.assert_close(outputs["out"], expected, rtol=0, atol=0)
+
+

inline_comments.body:
One case to check before dropping it: `TEGroupedMLP._ensure_main_grad` (`megatron/core/transformer/moe/experts.py`, from #5209) sets `overwrite_main_grad = True` on the expert weights in the op-fuser pre-forward hook whenever `fuse_wgrad_accumulation` is on and the attribute exists. When the unshard hooks run, for example with `optim` and FSDP units, the pre-backward gather resets the attribute to `_reduces_grad_every_backward(param)` before the fused wgrad reads it. Without the hook-time assignment, those expert wgrads would overwrite `main_grad` instead of accumulating across microbatches.

With this PR, the same thing can already happen under pure `no_shard`. The attribute now exists from construction, `_ensure_main_grad` flips it to `True`, and no hook resets it. Keeping the per-parameter policy in `_ensure_main_grad` instead of forcing `True` would cover both cases and make the hook-time assignment redundant. `test_make_fused_impl_pre_forward_hook_exposes_fsdp_main_grad_for_fused_wgrad` currently asserts the forced value.

I found this by reading the code; I haven't run the op-fuser grouped-MLP path.
